basis: Developmental brain disease and cardiac defects define syndrome; skeletal contractures in 2/2 and glaucoma in 1/2 support additional axes; samples small.
Defining brain abnormalities and neurodegeneration with dysosteosclerosis; optic atrophy and visual impairment only 1/4.
Defining cerebellar malformation; ectopic pituitary and low IGF1 in 2/2, impaired GH response in 1/2; strabismus and hypermetropia in 1/2. Small sample.
Defined autoinflammatory disease; supplied evidence does not establish specific additional organ damage or its frequency.
Inflammation damages the choroid, retina and vitreous; infectious or immune-mediated ocular disease.
Congenital immunodeficiency with defining polyclonal B-cell expansion, lymphoid hyperplasia and splenomegaly; recurrent infections do not establish lasting organ damage.
Suppurative infection of the renal collecting system.
Dermatophyte infection directly occupies and injures glabrous skin.
Aspergillus hypersensitivity causes bronchopulmonary inflammation and bronchiectasis; cortical atrophy annotation does not represent characteristic direct ABPA damage.
Inherited quantitative VWF deficiency causes a coagulation disorder; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish separate lasting organ damage.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining hepatic and cerebral dysfunction; renal tubular disease is a defining component, supporting renal involvement without a frequency estimate.
Defining intellectual disability and developmental delay; weakness in 2/5 does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.
Hereditary renal disease with preauricular pits; pits alone do not establish hearing or vestibular dysfunction.
Reported seizures and hemiparesis establish neurologic involvement; nonspecific skeletal abnormalities lack sufficient detail or frequency for another axis.
Tumour arises from meninges at the skull base; location alone does not establish bone, ocular or endocrine damage across the group.
Defining lacrimal, auditory and dental/salivary defects; digital malformations are also defining, with thumb phalanx duplication in 11/14.
Congenital absence of the heart directly defines the cardiovascular malformation.
Pulmonary venous/capillary vascular disease with defining infiltration of lung interstitium, bronchioles and pleura; impaired gas transfer is very frequent.
Defining skin appendage tumours; salivary neoplasms and hearing or visual damage occur in a small minority, below 30%.
Tuberculous infection directly damages bones or joints; pulmonary disease is not required for this extrapulmonary concept.
Inflammatory syndrome with developmental delay; persistent hyperkeratosis and skeletal deformities in reported 1/1 support involvement. Separate cancers excluded; frequency uncertain.
Loss of unilateral motor function usually reflects cerebral or other nervous system disease; paralysis alone does not establish intrinsic muscle disease.
Alveolar calcium-phosphate deposits directly injure lung tissue; right ventricular failure occurs in 5-29%, and extrapulmonary damaging deposits are rare.
Benign tumour arising from capillary blood vessels within the breast; its vascular origin falls within the cardiovascular axis.
Inherited phalangeal epiphyseal osteonecrosis with subsequent joint degeneration and restricted mobility.
